etymology: Blend of "-ism" + "automatic" - the label that fires before anything has been read.
occasion: A proposal that could be argued on its merits, and a room where the cheapest available reply is a word that ends the argument.
tell: Uses the word for a policy, a person and a sandwich in the same thread
Cannot define it when asked, but is certain who has it
The accusation grows as the argument is won
counter: Ask for the definition, then the instance: which policy, and which clause? An accusation that has to name a target stops being one.

confused_with.tell: Both fire without aiming; the ricochetoric fires claims, the ismatic fires labels, and neither has to defend a shot.
The xenophobricator blames the newest arrivals for a failure; the ismatic blames the proposal with the word that belongs to them. Both skip the mechanism.

senses: The pattern of accusing by label: socialist, communist, Marxist, groomer, woke - the word is fired at whatever is in front of it, so the accusation never has to survive a definition.
It works because the label is a loyalty test and not a claim: "socialist" here means "not one of us", which cannot be checked and therefore cannot be answered.
example: *"He called the library levy socialist, the zoning change communist and the flu shot Marxist, and could not define any of the three - a textbook **ismatic**, firing the word before reading the thing."*
